sentences.text: There will be time for you to read the instructions and questions and you'll have a chance to check your work.
sentences.zh: 您将有时间阅读说明和问题，而且您还有机会检查自己的答案。

sentences.text: Now turn to section 1.
sentences.zh: 现在请翻到第1部分。

sentences.text: Section 1. You will hear a man telephoning a library to find out about joining.
sentences.zh: 第1部分：您将听到一名男子打电话给图书馆，咨询入会事宜。

sentences.text: Section 2. You will see that there is an example which has been done for you.
sentences.zh: 第2部分：您会看到有一个已为您做好的示例。

sentences.text: On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
sentences.zh: 本次考试中，与该示例相关的对话将首先播放。

sentences.text: Good morning, North College Library. How can I help you?
sentences.zh: 早上好，北学院图书馆。请问有什么可以帮您的？

sentences.text: I was wondering if it was possible to join the library.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一下是否可以加入图书馆。

sentences.text: Are you a student at North College?
sentences.zh: 您是北学院的学生吗？

sentences.text: No, I'm not, but someone told me it was possible to join even if I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 不是，我不是。但有人告诉我，即使我不是学生，也可以加入。

sentences.text: That's right, it is. Are you over 18? That's our minimum joining age.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实可以。您年满18周岁了吗？这是我们入会的最低年龄要求。

sentences.text: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我已年满18周岁。

sentences.text: The minimum joining age is 18. So, 18 years has been written in the space.
sentences.zh: 入会最低年龄为18岁，因此空格处已填写‘18岁’。

sentences.text: Now we shall begin. You should answer the questions as you listen, because you will not hear the recording a second time.
sentences.zh: 现在考试开始。您需边听边答题，因为录音只播放一遍。

sentences.text: Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.
sentences.zh: 请仔细听，并回答第1至第5题。

sentences.text: Good morning, North College Library. How can I help you?
sentences.zh: 早上好，北学院图书馆。请问有什么可以帮您的？

sentences.text: I was wondering if it was possible to join the library.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一下是否可以加入图书馆。

sentences.text: Are you a student at North College? No, I'm not, but someone told me it was possible to join even if I wasn't.
sentences.zh: 您是北学院的学生吗？不是，我不是。但有人告诉我，即使我不是学生，也可以加入。

sentences.text: That's right, it is. Are you over 18? That's our minimum joining age.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实可以。您年满18周岁了吗？这是我们入会的最低年龄要求。

sentences.text: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我已年满18周岁。

sentences.text: That's no problem then.
sentences.zh: 那没问题了。

sentences.text: Could you tell me what I have to do to join?
sentences.zh: 您能告诉我加入需要做些什么吗？

sentences.text: Well, you'll need to come into the library and fill out some forms.
sentences.zh: 嗯，您需要来图书馆填写一些表格。

sentences.text: You'll also need to bring two passport photos with you.
sentences.zh: 您还需要带上两张护照照片。

sentences.text: We also need two documents for ID, so a driving license would be fine.
sentences.zh: 我们还需要两份身份证明文件，所以驾照就可以。

sentences.text: I've got that, and what else, a credit card?
sentences.zh: 我有驾照，还有别的吗？比如信用卡？

sentences.text: No, it needs to have your address on it.
sentences.zh: 不，证件上必须印有您的住址。

sentences.text: Shall I bring a bank statement with that, too?
sentences.zh: 那我再带一份银行对账单可以吗？

sentences.text: That'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 这样就可以了。

sentences.text: Good. Does it cost anything to join?
sentences.zh: 好的。加入需要付费吗？

sentences.text: Well, it's free for students here, but otherwise it's 125 pounds per year, or 25 pounds if you've got a current student card from another college.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里的学生是免费的，否则每年要125英镑，但如果您持有其他学院的有效学生证，则只需25英镑。

sentences.text: I was at Westerley College until last year, but now I've got a job at Jefferson's steel factory.
sentences.zh: 我去年之前在韦斯特利学院读书，但现在我在杰斐逊钢铁厂工作。

sentences.text: It's more expensive than I thought.
sentences.zh: 这比我想的要贵。

sentences.text: My local library is free.
sentences.zh: 我家附近的图书馆是免费的。

sentences.text: But you'll find they don't have the range of reference books or facilities, which we buy for our students.
sentences.zh: 但您会发现，他们没有我们为学生采购的那么丰富的参考书和设施。

sentences.text: That's why you have to pay to be an external member.
sentences.zh: 因此，外部会员需要付费。

sentences.text: I see. How many books can I borrow?
sentences.zh: 我明白了。我可以借多少本书？

sentences.text: We allow 12 items borrowed at any one time if you're a student, and that includes CDs, DVDs and videos.
sentences.zh: 作为学生，我们允许您同时借阅12件物品，其中包括CD、DVD和录像带。

sentences.text: However, it's only eight items for members of the public.
sentences.zh: 不过，公众会员只能借阅8件物品。

sentences.text: Fine. And how long can I have them for?
sentences.zh: 好的。那我能借多久？

sentences.text: Well, you can have both fiction and reference books for four weeks, which isn't bad, really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，小说类和参考类图书都可以借阅四周，其实这已经很不错了。

sentences.text: And what happens if I return them late?
sentences.zh: 如果我逾期归还，会发生什么？

sentences.text: Like all libraries, there's a fine system in place. The minimum fine is £150, but it can be much higher for some items up to £5 per week.
sentences.zh: 和所有图书馆一样，我们实行罚款制度。最低罚款为150英镑，但某些物品的罚款可能更高，最高可达每周5英镑。

sentences.text: We'll give you a booklet with all the details when you join.
sentences.zh: 您入会时，我们会为您提供一本包含所有详细信息的小册子。

sentences.text: You can always renew items if they're not required by anyone else by telephone or logging onto our website.
sentences.zh: 只要没有其他读者预约，您就可以通过电话或登录我们的网站续借图书。

sentences.text: What about the computers? Can I use them free of charge?
sentences.zh: 那电脑呢？我可以免费使用吗？

sentences.text: For college students it's free, but for external members like yourself, the first hour is free, and then we make a nominal charge of money.
sentences.zh: 对学院学生是免费的，但对您这样的外部会员，首小时免费，之后仅收取象征性费用。

sentences.text: Do I have to book an advance for them?
sentences.zh: 我需要提前预约电脑吗？

sentences.text: Oh, yes, it's advisable. Most people tend to book 24 hours in advance, although sometimes you can get one with only six hours notice.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，建议您提前预约。大多数人通常会提前24小时预约，不过有时仅提前6小时也能预约到。

sentences.text: However, the earliest you can book a computer is 48 hours before you need it, and you can only book one hour at a time.
sentences.zh: 但您最早只能在需要使用电脑前48小时进行预约，且每次最多只能预约一小时。

sentences.text: If no one else has done it, then you can go to the library and write a book for the library.
sentences.zh: 如果没有其他人预约，您可直接前往图书馆，并为图书馆撰写一本书。

sentences.text: The earliest you can book a computer is 48 hours before you need it, and you can only book one hour at a time.
sentences.zh: 最早您可以在需要使用电脑前48小时进行预约，且每次只能预约一小时。

sentences.text: If no one else has booked the computer out, then you may be able to have another hour if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果没有其他人已预约该电脑，您可能可以再额外使用一小时。

sentences.text: We have a wide range of databases, so the computers are in great demand.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有大量数据库，因此电脑需求量很大。

sentences.text: I'm thinking of doing some writing, and I might need to access national newspapers.
sentences.zh: 我打算写些东西，可能需要查阅全国性报纸。

sentences.text: Do you have them on these databases?
sentences.zh: 这些数据库里有全国性报纸吗？

sentences.text: We do indeed. We've got all the big nationals, the guardian, and the observer, the independent, and the times, and some times.
sentences.zh: 确实有。我们收录了所有主流全国性报纸，包括《卫报》《观察家报》《独立报》《泰晤士报》，以及部分《星期日泰晤士报》。

sentences.text: We've also got all the local papers, and a wide selection of magazines.
sentences.zh: 我们还收录了所有地方性报纸，以及大量杂志。

sentences.text: Excellent. I assume you have photocopy facilities.
sentences.zh: 太好了。我想你们应该提供复印服务吧？

sentences.text: Of course. Five-pier sheet for both A4 and A3 black and white copies, and 40-pier sheet for colour.
sentences.zh: 当然提供。A4和A3尺寸的黑白复印均为每张5便士，彩色复印为每张40便士。

sentences.text: You can get a card from the counter here, it doesn't take coins.
sentences.zh: 您可在此柜台领取复印卡，该卡不接受硬币。

sentences.text: Okay. Oh, by the way, another thing I was wondering about was if you ran any writing classes through the library.
sentences.zh: 好的。哦，对了，我还想问一下，你们图书馆是否开设写作课程？

sentences.text: We do, but you'll have to speak to John Granting him about that. He's our resident author. He runs the creative writing classes.
sentences.zh: 我们有开设，但您需要跟约翰·格兰廷先生联系此事。他是我们的驻馆作家，负责创意写作课程。

sentences.text: John Granting. Could you spell that for me, please?
sentences.zh: 约翰·格兰廷。麻烦您帮我拼写一下这个名字，好吗？

sentences.text: Certainly. G-R-A-N-T-I-N-G-H-A-M.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。G-R-A-N-T-I-N-G-H-A-M。

sentences.text: Are the classes here at the library?
sentences.zh: 这些课程是在图书馆内进行吗？

sentences.text: Yes, he's here on Thursday evenings. Oh, no. Sorry. Friday. He's just changed it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他每周四晚上在这里授课。哦，不，抱歉，改到周五了。他刚刚调整了时间。

sentences.text: You can contact him by emailing the library.
sentences.zh: 您可以通过向图书馆发送电子邮件来联系他。

sentences.text: Okay. Right. Well, that's about all I need to know.
sentences.zh: 好的，明白了。那么，我需要了解的情况大致就这些了。

sentences.text: Thank you. I'll be a long later this week to join. Thanks. Bye.
sentences.zh: 谢谢！我这周晚些时候会过来报名参加。谢谢，再见。

sentences.text: Now turn to section two.
sentences.zh: 现在请翻到第二部分。

sentences.text: Section 2
sentences.zh: 第二部分

sentences.text: You will hear a man called Dan Perman
sentences.zh: 您将听到一位名叫丹·珀尔曼的男士

sentences.text: talking on the radio about pedal power, a UK charity which sends bicycles to people in developing countries.
sentences.zh: 在电台中介绍‘踏板动力’（Pedal Power）——一家将自行车运送给发展中国家民众的英国慈善机构。

sentences.text: My name is Dan Perman and I'd like to talk about the work of pedal power, a small charity based mainly in the UK.
sentences.zh: 我叫丹·珀尔曼，今天想为大家介绍一下‘踏板动力’这家慈善机构的工作情况。这是一家规模较小、总部主要设在英国的慈善组织。

sentences.text: I'll be giving our contact details at the end if anyone would like to find out more about how to support us.
sentences.zh: 最后我会提供我们的联系方式，如果您想进一步了解如何支持我们，欢迎随时联系我们。

sentences.text: But first, how the charity began.
sentences.zh: 但首先，让我们了解一下这家慈善机构的创立缘起。

sentences.text: I got the idea of exporting bicycles to developing countries while I was in Ecuador.
sentences.zh: 我在厄瓜多尔时萌生了向发展中国家出口自行车的想法。

sentences.text: I went there in 1993 just after graduating from university.
sentences.zh: 我于1993年大学毕业后前往厄瓜多尔。

sentences.text: After three years of studying, I wanted adventure.
sentences.zh: 经过三年的学习，我渴望一场冒险。

sentences.text: I loved traveling, so I decided to join a voluntary organisation and was sent Ecuador to carry out land surveys.
sentences.zh: 我热爱旅行，因此决定加入一家志愿组织，并被派往厄瓜多尔开展土地勘测工作。

sentences.text: The project came to an end after five years and when I returned to the UK in 1998, I started planning pedal power.
Where I lived in Ecuador was a very rural area.
My neighbour had the only bicycle in the village, whereas everyone else walked everywhere.
My neighbour's business was unusually successful, and for years I couldn't understand why.
Then I realized having a bike meant he could get where he wanted to go without much trouble.
Other local carpenters could only accept jobs in a three-kilometer radius, so no matter how skilled they were, they could never do as many jobs as my neighbour.
At pedal power, we collect second hand bikes in the UK and send them to some of the poorest regions in the world.
When we distribute bikes overseas, we don't give them away for free.
We'd like to, but long-term that doesn't really help the local economy.
The demand for bikes is enormous, which makes them very expensive locally.
So we sell them for 5% of the normal price.
But in order to continue operating, we need to have a constant supply of bikes which we send out every six months.
One example of a town that's received bicycles from pedal power is Rivas.
It was the first place I send a full container of bicycles to.
Most people there now earn a bicycle.
The local economy has developed so much, you wouldn't recognise it as the same place.
In fact, there are more bikes than on the streets of Amsterdam, if you've ever been there.
But pedal power still needs your help.
You may have read about some of our recent problems in the British media.
In August 2000, we simply ran out of money.
We had containers of bikes ready to send, but no money to pay the bills.
It was a terrible situation.
We managed to ensure the bikes went out on time, but the other problems carried on for several months.
Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.
Fortunately in October 2001, we won an Enterprise Award, which helped us enormously.
We invested 15 of the 75,000 pound prize money to help secure our future.
Winning the award held raise our profile, and the money enabled us to pay all our shipping costs, which represent our greatest expense.
Pedal power changes lives. When someone gets a bicycle from us, they see a 14% increase in their income.
We're currently looking to invest in computers so that our office staff can do an even better job.
Because of our work, people in a number of countries now have a better standard of living.
So far we've provided 46,000 people with bikes.
But we'd like to send more, at least 50,000 by the end of the year.
Now there are many ways in which you can support the work of pedal power, not just by taking a bike to a collection in your area.
I should also like to say, if you do have a bike to donate, it doesn't matter what condition it's in.
If we can't repair it, we'll strip it down for spare parts.
Of course, to do that, we'll always need tools which are expensive to buy, so we welcome any that you can give.
Also, you could help by contacting the voluntary staff at our offices.
They'll be able to suggest activities you could organize to bring in funds for us.
People do all kinds of things, including of course, sponsored bike rides.
Also, we're always interested to hear of other places that would benefit from receiving a concimement of bikes,
and welcome suggestions from people who've been to developing regions on their travels.
We hope that by talking on radio programs like this, we will be able to raise public awareness,
which will lead to government organizations also giving us regular financial support, something that we really need.
If you'd like some more information about where to donate an old bicycle, or offer help in other ways, please contact us.
That is the end of section two.
You now have half a minute to check your answers.
Now turn to section three.
Section 3 You will hear a discussion between a college tutor and two students, Christina and Ibrahim.
First of all, I'd just like to say Christina and Ibrahim that I really enjoyed watching your video about student life last week.
And I can see that the rest of the group did too. You did really well.
And I hope that you got a lot out of it. I'd like to use this tutorial as a feedback session where you reflect on the experience of doing the project.
So Christina, I was wondering what did you enjoy most about making the video?
I liked using the camera.
Is it the first time you've operated one like that?
Yes it is.
Well the results were very good. Anything else?
I also enjoyed visiting one of the British students we filmed. I'd never been inside a British home before.
Okay Christina, thanks. What about you Ibrahim? What did you enjoy?

Well for me it was a very good chance to get to know students who are on other courses because everyone in our group is studying English and we don't usually have much to do with the rest of the college.
Yes good. Do you think you'll maintain the contact now?
I hope so. I've invited three of them to have dinner with me next week.
Great. If you haven't decided what to make yet I can tell you they are love trying Arab dishes.
And of course it's good for your English too.
Christina, what did you find? What was the most useful aspect of the project from the point of view of the English practice?
I think when we were being shown how to edit the film we had to follow the instructions and that was very good practice for me.
And I also learned some technical words that I hadn't heard before.
Hmm. What about you Ibrahim? What was the most useful for your English?
It was listening to the British students because they don't speak as slowly as most of the tutors are of course.
I think they speak at natural speed so it forces me to get used to it and they use a lot of slang.
So you learn some new words which will be useful? Yes.
Good. I'm glad it helped.
Well we've talked a little bit about enjoyment and about language practice where there are any other benefits.
What else did you feel you'd learn from the project? Was it useful in other ways?
Yes. Well firstly I learned how to use a video camera and also I think I really learned a lot about working together with other people.
I've never done anything with a group before and we had to find ways of cooperating and compromising and sometimes persuading people when they don't agree with you.
Yes. That is a very useful experience I know.
Now listen and answer questions 27 to 30.

What about you, Ebrahim? Well I think I learned a lot about how important editing is when you're filming you think that everything is going to be interesting but in fact we cut around half of it in the end and then it was much better.
Good. Well one last thing I'd like to ask.
What mistakes do you think you as a group that is made? I mean to put it another way if you had to do it all over again is there anything you do differently?

We didn't plan very well. For example we didn't decide on dates when we'd complete each separate step of the project and we should have agreed about that in the beginning because we were always late with everything.
Right. Anything else?
I think we should have tried to experiment more with the camera. I mean with angles and the focus and that kind of thing.
So you should have been more ambitious. Do you agree, Ebrahim?

Not really. In fact I think we were too ambitious. We were in experience and we didn't have a lot of time and we tried to do too much to make a long film. Next time I would make a shorter one and try to get the quality better.
Well that's very interesting. Next semester we will be doing another video project with a different content of course.
But you'll have an opportunity to put into practice what you've learned this time.
Do you have any ideas about...
That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
Now turn to section four.
Section 4 You will hear a talk about scientific research in the continent of Antarctica.
Tonight I'm going to talk to you about that remarkable continent Antarctica.
Remote, hostile, and at present uninhabited on a permanent basis.
For early explorers, it was the ultimate survival contest.
For researchers like me, it remains a place of great intellectual challenge.
While for the modern tourist, it's simply a wilderness of great beauty.
First, some facts and figures.
Antarctica is a place of extremes.
The highest, coldest and windiest continent, and over 58 times the size of the UK.
The ice cap contains almost 70% of the world's fresh water, and 90% of its ice.
But with very low snowfall, most of the continent technically falls unbelievably into the category of desert.
Huge icebergs break off the continent each year.
While in winter, half the surrounding ocean frees is over, which means it's size almost doubles.
Research and exploration has been going on in Antarctica for more than 200 years,
and has involved scientists from many different countries who work together on research stations.
Here, science and technical support have been integrated in a very cost-effective way.
Our Antarctic Research Program has several summers only stations and two all year round ones.
I was based on one of the all year round ones.
The research stations are really self-contained communities of about 20 people.
There's living and working space, a kitchen with a huge food store, a small hospital, and a well equipped gym,
to ensure everyone keeps fit in their spare time.
The station generates its own electricity, and communicates with the outside world using a satellite link.
Our station, zero one, had some special features.
It wasn't built on land, but on an ice shelf, hundreds of meters thick.
Supplies were brought to us on large sledge's from a ship 15 kilometers away at the Ice Age.
Living in the Antarctic hasn't always been so comfortable.
Snow buildups caused enormous problems for four previous stations on the same site,
which were buried and finally crushed by the weight.
Fortunately, no one was hurt, but these buildings became a huge challenge to architects,
who finally came up with a remarkable solution.
The buildings are placed on platforms, which can be raised above the changing snow level,
on legs which are extendable.
Food is one of the most important aspects of survival in a polar climate.
People living there need to obtain a lot more energy from their food, both to keep warm,
and to undertake heavy physical work.
Maybe you know that an adult in the UK will probably need about 1,700 kilocalories a day on average.
Someone in Antarctica will need about 3,500, just over double.
This energy is provided by foods which are high in carbohydrate and fat.
Rations for field work present an additional problem.
They need to provide maximum energy, but they must also be compact and light for easy transport.
Special boxes are prepared, each containing enough food for one person for 20 days.
You may be familiar with coffee processed by freeze drying, which preserves the quality of the food product,
while making a large saving in weight.
Well, this type of presentation is ideal in our situation.
It wasn't available to earlier polar explorers whose diet was commonly insufficient for their health.
I think that being at the cutting edge of science has a special appeal for everyone working in Antarctica in whatever capacity.
As a marine biologist, my own research was fascinating, but it's perhaps climate change research that is the most crucial field of study.
Within this general field, surveying changes in the volume and stability of the ice cap is vital,
since these may have profound effects on world sea levels and on ocean currents.
A second important area is monitoring the size of the hole in the ozone layer above Antarctica,
since this is an indicator of global ultraviolet radiation levels.
Thirdly, bubbles in the ice sheet itself provide an index of pollution,
because frozen inside them are samples of previous atmospheres over the past 500,000 years.
And these providers with evidence for the effects of such human activities as agriculture and industry.
There are an increasing number of opportunities for young people to work for a period in Antarctica,
not only as research assistants and projects like mine, but also in a wide range of junior administrative and technical positions,
including vacancies for matte makers.
I hope that the insights I've provided will encourage you to take up these opportunities in this fascinating continent.
Let us see the end of section 4.
You now have half a minute to check your answers.
That is the end of the listening test.
In the IELTS test, you would now have 10 minutes to transfer your answers to the listening answer sheet.
